maml:description.maml:para: Returns an object of Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributables for use with other VcRedist functions.

This function returns Visual C++ Redistributable entries from a manifest as objects that can be passed to other VcRedist functions. It does not check which Redistributables are installed; use Get-InstalledVcRedist for that.

By default, `-Source Auto` reads the bundled manifest and tries the remote manifest from the VcRedist repository. It uses the remote manifest if valid and at least as recent as the bundled manifest; otherwise it uses the bundled manifest. An unavailable or invalid remote manifest produces a warning; an unreadable or invalid bundled manifest causes an error. Use `-Source Bundled` for repeatable offline runs.

The Release and Architecture parameters select matching entries regardless of support status; a warning is emitted if any selected entries are unsupported. Without these parameters, the command selects release 14 for x86, x64, and arm64. Use `-Export Supported` or `-Export Unsupported` to select entries across releases by support status, or `-Export All` to return all entries. The Export parameter cannot be combined with Release or Architecture. The All and Unsupported export modes always emit a warning, even if the selected manifest contains no unsupported entries.

The returned objects include the manifest properties, including Supported, URI, and SupportedArchitecture. In SilentUninstall, the #Installer and #ProductCode placeholders are replaced with the installer filename from URI and the entry's product code.
The internal manifest can be exported with Export-VcManifest.

maml:description.maml:para: Packages the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable installers into intunewin format and imports as applications into a Microsoft Intune tenant.

Creates an application in a Microsoft Intune tenant for each Visual C++ Redistributable and includes properties such as target Silent command, Uninstall command, Detection (via Registry) and Requirements.
Use Get-VcList and Save-VcRedist to download the Redistributables and create the array for importing into Microsoft Intune.

An application package will be created for each Visual C++ Redistributable with properties including Name, Description, Publisher, App Version, Information URL, Privacy URL, Notes, Logo, Install command, Uninstall command, Install behavior, Operating system architecture, Minimum operating system, and Detection rules.

This function requires the IntuneWin32App PowerShell module and supported Windows PowerShell only. Before using this function to import the Redistributables into an Intune tenant, authenticate first with Connect-MSIntuneGraph. The architecture requirement comes from each manifest entry's SupportedArchitecture list. IntuneWin32App 1.5.0 supports the ARM64-inclusive requirements used by the bundled manifest; unsupported combinations are rejected. Existing applications are not changed unless an update is imported.

Use `-ImportAsUpdate` to add a file-version requirement based on each package's `DetectionFile`. The app is applicable only when the architecture-specific file exists and is older than the package version. It is not applicable to clean installs or devices with the same or a newer version. This does not change existing Intune apps or their assignments. Verify the detection file and version on target devices, particularly for older, unsupported redistributables that may use side-by-side assemblies. A remote manifest can provide different detection paths from the bundled manifest.

maml:description.maml:para: Installs the Visual C++ Redistributables on the local system.

Installs the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributables from a list created by Get-VcList and downloaded into a folder structure locally with Save-VcRedist. Supports both passive and silent installation of the Redistributables. Useful for Windows deployments including creating gold images via HashiCorp Packer where the Redistributables can be downloaded and installed at runtime. The function requires an elevated PowerShell session. Installers whose manifest SupportedArchitecture list does not include the native Windows architecture are skipped with a warning. Use -Force to re-install an already installed redistributable or to install an x64 redistributable on an ARM64 operating system despite the manifest architecture check. Each input object must include a non-empty SupportedArchitecture list. All input is collected before installation and sorted by the release order in the bundled manifest, then by version within each release. Releases missing from that order are rejected.

maml:description.maml:para: Uninstall the installed Visual C++ Redistributables on the local system.

Uninstall the specified Release and/or Architecture of the installed Visual C++ Redistributables on the local system. The command requires an elevated PowerShell session. Without parameters, it selects the default releases for x86 and x64. Use Release and Architecture to filter installed entries, or pass objects from Get-InstalledVcRedist or Get-VcList through the pipeline.

When both Release and Architecture are explicitly specified, each selected combination with no installed match returns a result with State `Not installed` and null Name, Version, and ExitCode properties. If either parameter is omitted, no such results are generated for missing combinations.

For pipeline input with a missing executable uninstaller, the command checks the product code against installed entries. An absent product is reported as `Not installed`; a missing uninstaller for an installed product, or an input without a product code, is reported as `Failed` with a warning. Exit code 1605 is also reported as `Not installed`.
The command supports WhatIf and Confirm. Checks performed before an uninstall is attempted can still produce `Not installed` or `Failed` results with WhatIf.
Specifies the releases of the Redistributables to uninstall. Accepted values are 2005, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2022, and 14. Release 14 identifies the unified 2015-2022+ runtime.
Specifies the processor architectures of the Redistributables to uninstall: x86, x64, or ARM64. ARM64 must be specified explicitly.

State is `Uninstalled` for exit codes 0, 1641, or 3010; `Not installed` for exit code 1605 or the missing selections described above; and `Failed` for a missing uninstaller or an unsuccessful process. ExitCode is null when no process was run. Exit code 1641 indicates a restart was initiated, and 3010 indicates a restart is required.

maml:description.maml:para: Updates existing Visual C++ Redistributable applications in a Microsoft Deployment Toolkit share.

Finds existing MDT applications by their short name and updates the installer content and application properties when the manifest version, product code, or install command has changed. It does not create missing applications. The function requires Windows PowerShell 5.1 and the Microsoft Deployment Toolkit module.
This function is deprecated because Microsoft no longer supports MDT. It emits a warning and may be removed in a future release of VcRedist.
